decisions.reason: As a close-to-core handle product already placed on the website, it fits the firm's broad established offer and there is no reported failure strong enough to overcome the tendency to continue a recent launch.

A handle family suggests a somewhat broader development and portfolio commitment than a single item, so management is likely to keep it unless clear negative evidence emerges, which is not reported here.
This design variant is near the firm's core business and publicly marketed, so with no explicit disappointing results the firm is likely to retain it rather than admit an early mistake.
Like the other new handle designs, it is an incremental extension of the established range and there is no sign of persistent poor performance that would justify withdrawal despite prior commitment.

Because it is a product family close to the core assortment, it supports the firm's system breadth and is likely to be continued given sunk development effort and no stated evidence of underperformance.

This electronic access system is strongly aligned with the firm's announced move toward digital building organization and was promoted with a specific launch claim, making withdrawal especially unlikely under escalation of commitment.
